rationale:
Evidence: iteration 6 (sensor_size 0.016, kp 4.5, kd 1.0, ki 0.05, mass 0.6, body_length 0.11) is the best design at 945.42, with 20/20 finishes on all three development tracks, progress about 0.996 to 0.998 and rms_error about 0.006. Iteration 8 (kp 5.0) scored 945.14, within noise, so higher kp has stopped helping. Iteration 9 (kd 1.2) fell to 941.04, with higher oval oscillation, so kd 1.0 is near its useful limit. Iteration 7 (mass 0.5, base_speed 0.95) was worse, so lighter mass and more speed are not the lever.

Remaining score headroom is small: line_loss_events (about 0.1 to 0.5 per run, about 15 points each) and completion time (about 2 points per 0.1 s). Most of the gain has already been taken from geometry.

Change: revert to the iteration 6 design (kp 4.5, kd 1.0, sensor_size 0.016, mass 0.6, body_length 0.11, base_speed 0.9) and raise ki from 0.05 to 0.10. The aim is to pull the robot back onto the line on the slalom and s-bend drift, which should lower line_loss_events and max_error. The integral is clamped at +/-2, so windup risk is limited at this value. Everything else is unchanged, so the effect of ki is attributable.

Hypotheses: H1, a small ki reduces the sustained lateral drift on bends (the slalom has the highest oscillation and line losses), so line_loss_events falls below 0.3. H2, if steering_oscillation or control_effort rises with no line-loss gain, ki is past its useful range and the final design should return to ki 0.05.

Expected result: score about 945 to 950, with completion held at 100 percent on all tracks. Measurements wanted: line_loss_events, max_error and completion_time per track, and steering_oscillation and control_effort to check that ki adds no jitter.
